hints: Find radius $BC = \sqrt{6^2 + 6^2} = 6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$ and angle $\frac{\pi}{4}\text{ rad}$.
walkthrough:
In right-angled triangle $\triangle OBC$ (with $OB = 6\text{ cm}$ and $OC = 6\text{ cm}$), calculate the radius $BC$ of the circle centred at $B$:
$$BC = \sqrt{OB^2 + OC^2} = \sqrt{6^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{72} = 6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$$

Determine the central angle $\angle OBC$ in radians:
$$\angle OBC = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{OC}{OB}\right) = \tan^{-1}(1) = \frac{\pi}{4}\text{ radians}$$

Calculate the circular arc length $DC$:
$$\text{Arc } DC = r_B\theta = 6\sqrt{2} \times \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{3\sqrt{2}\pi}{2} \approx 6.6643 \approx 6.66\text{ cm} \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$

ai_rubric.Arc Length: Finds radius $6\sqrt{2}$ (M1). Applies $s = r\theta$ with angle $\pi/4$ (M1). Obtains $6.66\text{ cm}$ (A1).

skill_tags: Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regions

walkthrough:
Calculate the area of circular sector $BDC$ (radius $6\sqrt{2}$, angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$):
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } BDC) = \frac{1}{2}(6\sqrt{2})^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{2}(72)\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = 9\pi\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of region $Q$ by subtracting triangle $\triangle OBC$ from sector $BDC$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle OBC) = \frac{1}{2}(6)(6) = 18\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Area}(Q) = 9\pi - 18\text{ cm}^2 \quad (\approx 10.2743)$$

Calculate the area of region $P$ by subtracting region $Q$ from the semicircle quadrant $BOC$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{quadrant } BOC) = \frac{1}{4}\pi(6^2) = 9\pi\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Area}(P) = 9\pi - (9\pi - 18) = 18\text{ cm}^2$$

Compute the ratio of the areas:
$$\frac{\text{Area}(P)}{\text{Area}(Q)} = \frac{18}{9\pi - 18} = \frac{2}{\pi - 2} \approx \frac{2}{1.14159} \approx 1.7519 \approx 1.75 \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$

ai_rubric.Area Ratio: Finds sector $BDC = 9\pi$ (M1). Computes Area $Q = 9\pi - 18$ (DM1). Computes Area $P = 18$ (M1). Obtains ratio $1.75$ (A1).
